question: When a rewritten rung scores below verbatim, is that information the rewrite removed, or language understanding the submission lacks?

reference_version.hash_policy: run.py refuses to run when the live perturb.py or metrics.py hashes differ from these; the transforms are the benchmark's own, imported unmodified.

seeds.note: pool_seed permutes the enumerated candidate pool into query order (numpy RandomState, machine-stable); tie_break_seed is passed to language_search_benchmark.metrics.rank_matrix, the benchmark's own tie-break.

family_counts.note: The real perturb.STOPWORDS contains 'near', so the keywords rung deletes the relation word on all 8 near-scene queries; the truncated rung inherits the same deletion. This is measured, not assumed: see results/identifiability.json.

rungs.mirror: retrieval-v4 scores the rewritten rungs and reports verbatim; the study keeps that split.

systems.exact-grammar: grammar-aware decoding (unique in-vocabulary typo correction) with attribute-overlap scoring; the conditional-identifiability ceiling system
systems.lexical-idf: IDF-weighted bag-of-words cosine over the frozen candidate corpus with the course's zero-vector rule for unseen words; the course's own mechanism, miniature and offline
systems.small-adapters: registered cogworks.submissions.v2 entry points; discovered at run time, run only if importable offline. None were registered in the study environment, so this baseline is recorded as not run.

metrics.raw_ranks: per system, per rung, per query: 1-based rank of the gold candidate in the whole 40-candidate pool plus the top answer
metrics.justified_answer_coverage: fraction of queries whose top answer is compatible with the rewritten query under the system's own decoder; an incompatible answer used information the query does not carry
metrics.byte_identical_rewrite_ambiguities: per rung: queries whose rewrite equals their own verbatim string, and collision groups of queries sharing one identical rewrite byte string
metrics.identifiability: compatible-set size distributions under lexical and grammar-aware decoding, with the implied E[MRR] ceilings

data_provenance: Fully synthetic grammar text. No COCO captions, no course data files, no content from language_search_benchmark/manifests/public-*.json, and no code or results from the language-validity study. Its queries and candidates are generated by experiments/query-information/grammar.py alone.
limits: The finite grammar gives conditional identifiability inside that grammar: what a rewritten query still determines over these 40 candidates. It is not general semantic truth, and nothing here is a new official scorer or a change to metrics.py, perturb.py, or the benchmark manifests.
